newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to keep Eurobond tax exemption law - sources.
newsitem.headline: MOF to keep Eurobond tax exemption law - sources.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance will maintain the withholding tax exemption law for foreigners on income gains made from Japanese bonds issued overseas, including Eurobonds, until the end of March 1998, government and industry sources said on Thursday.
"The Liberal Democratic Party's (LDP) tax panel and MOF have decided to simply extend the current tax exemption law for one more year," an industry official said.
The law, which is reviewed every two years, would expire at the end of the current fiscal year without an extension.
An official at MOF's Tax Bureau had said that the ministry did not intend to keep the law in its current form and wanted to attach certain conditions.

MOF officials have said they want to close a loophole which gives a tax break on Euroyen purchases by Japanese investors who buy the bonds through the overseas subsidiaries of Japanese financial institutions.
Last week, MOF disclosed a plan to require foreigners to identify themselves in order to be exempt from paying a withholding tax, but various industries opposed the plan.
MOF and the LDP's tax panel have been discussing the issue since last week. They are expected to formally announce an extension by December 20.
MOF will work with various industries to come up with a compromise acceptable to market participants, and aim to come up with a rule by the end of the 1997/98 fiscal year, they said.

MOF is eager to come up with a way to stop tax evasion by Japanese investors before it becomes too late as cross-border trading will be able to be conducted with little regulation when the current foreign exchange law is revised in early 1998.
The abolition of the current 40-day lock-up rule on domestic sales of Euroyen bonds issued by Japanese borrowers is also making MOF nervous, industry sources said.
The lock-up rule bans brokers from selling Euroyen bonds to Japanese residents for 40 days after the launch of the bond.

"We expect an opportunity will be made for MOF and officials from various industries to get together around the table to come up with a constructive solution to resolve the matter as quickly as possible," a MOF official said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
